newsitem.title: FRANCE: France protests at assault on ambassador in Congo.
newsitem.headline: France protests at assault on ambassador in Congo.

text.p: France called in the Congolese envoy in Paris on Thursday to protest against an assault on its ambassador in the Congo capital Brazzaville.
"We lodged an immediate protest with the Congo ambassador in Paris," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
Panicky troops loyal to President Pascal Lissouba asssaulted French ambassador Raymond Cesaire on Wednesday in Brazzaville as the envoy tried to leave Lissouba's palace after a meeting.
Cesaire's bodyguard was beaten up and his escort fired upon.

The incident occurred as troops loyal to Lissouba and militia backing former president Denis Sassou Nguesso battled for the city's airport. Both sides claimed on Thursday morning to control the strategic location.
Asked if Paris now planned to close its embassy in Brazzaville, Rummelhardt told reporters this was not planned.
"We are hoping the mediation now under way will succeed," he said at the ministry's daily briefing.
Fighting erupted in Brazzaville on June 5 and has left 1,000 to 3,000 people dead.
